stem: An adult woman with acute uncomplicated cystitis is prescribed fosfomycin tromethamine granules for oral solution. Which teaching by the nurse is correct?

options.A: Dissolve the contents of one prescribed sachet in water and take it as a single oral dose.
options.B: Take one sachet every day until urinary symptoms completely resolve.
options.C: Swallow the dry granules directly because mixing with water reduces absorption.
options.D: Expect the medication to be administered only by intravenous infusion for uncomplicated cystitis.

rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed labeling states that for women 18 years of age and older with uncomplicated urinary tract infection (acute cystitis), the recommended dose is one sachet of fosfomycin tromethamine granules for oral solution. The contents must be dissolved in water and taken orally. The label also warns not to use repeated daily doses for a single episode because repeated dosing did not improve clinical or microbiologic success and increased adverse events. B therefore gives an unsupported multidose regimen. C contradicts the preparation instructions. D is incorrect because this labeled product is an oral granule formulation.
educational_objective: Teach correct administration of oral fosfomycin tromethamine for acute uncomplicated cystitis: one prescribed sachet is dissolved in water and taken as a single oral dose rather than repeated daily or swallowed dry.
source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
source_document_title: Fosfomycin Tromethamine Granules for Oral Solution Prescribing Information
source_locator: Dosage and Administration: recommended dosage for women 18 years and older with uncomplicated UTI (acute cystitis) is one sachet; Preparation: dissolve the entire contents of the single-dose sachet in water and take orally; General precaution: do not use more than one single dose for one episode because repeated daily doses did not improve outcomes and increased adverse events.
source_claim_supported: For labeled treatment of acute uncomplicated cystitis in adult women, fosfomycin tromethamine granules are administered as one oral sachet dissolved in water; repeated daily dosing for the same episode is not recommended.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing

correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item around the exact current FDA-label administration instructions. Removed the vague pharmacokinetic rationale and used the directly supported single-dose, oral, dissolve-in-water requirements without inventing additional treatment duration.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against the April 9, 2026 DailyMed label and current 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A exactly matches labeled dose/form/preparation. B contradicts the no-repeat-daily-dose warning. C contradicts the requirement to dissolve the granules. D misstates the route/formulation.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; one sachet dissolved in water and taken orally as a single dose.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; repeated daily doses are not recommended for one acute cystitis episode.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; the granules should not be swallowed dry.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; the labeled product is oral.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The stem specifies the labeled population and uncomplicated cystitis, leaving one clear administration answer.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address route/preparation/dosing for the same drug.
audit_findings.blueprint: Medication-administration teaching directly fits Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked population, route, preparation, single-dose instruction, and repeated-dose warning against current labeling. Removed unsupported pharmacokinetic explanations and found no second defensible answer.
